newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Telmex pops as stock holds 35.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Telmex pops as stock holds 35.

text.p: Options on ADRs of Telefonos de Mexico SA were active for a second day as the stock held above the key 35 strike level.
In afternoon trading, Telmex was up 5/8 at 36-1/2 on consolidated volume of more than six million shares. The stock closed 2-1/2 points higher Monday.
"We've broken out of a range. This is nice," Scott Kilrea at LETCO in Chicago said.
Monday's close put the stock at its highest level since late April last year. It spent most of the year bouncing between roughly 30 and 34.
"Telmex for the last year hasn't really strayed far off 30," Kilrea said. "It was acting like a utility company, not a Mexican stock. It's nice to see it break through a strike."
Most Telmex options traded at the 35 strike price. Roughly 8,300 Telmex January 35 calls traded on four options exchanges. The same put traded 4,185 contracts.
Most of that volume was on the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"Everybody wants them," Kilrea said of the January 35s. "Every month they just get sold and sold and sold.
"There was a large contingent of people that were short them and now they need to buy them back," he said. "There's another contingent finally liking the prem and selling the 35s."
The February and May 35 calls also drew heavy activity, with the February 35 call trading a total of 1,755 and the May 35 trading 1,520.
The February and May 40 calls also saw solid interest.
In other activity, the American Express Co January 50 puts and calls each traded 10,000 contracts.
Traders said the action was a conversion done against a million shares of stock.
American Express options trade on the American Stock Exchange and CBOE. The 10,000 contracts crossed on the American Stock Exchange.
American Express shares were up 2-1/2 at 57-5/8 Tuesday afternoon.
Also on the American Stock Exchange, the CompUSA Inc February 22-1/2 call traded 9,756 contracts in one block. The option crossed at 1/4, up 1/16.
CompUSA shares added 7/8 to 14-3/4.
Activity in Zitel Corp cooled from the recent heavy pace, but traders said volatility remained high as the stock continued to trade in fairly wide ranges.
Zitel shares bounced between 47 and 52-1/8 Tuesday and had settled in at 48, down 3/8, by afternoon trading.
"They're still playing Zitel volatility," said Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities in Chicago.
"The volatilities are huge in here but things keep bouncing around," he said. "There are a lot of speculators in it." ((G.Crawford, 3124088750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
